notes: 1916 four-storey flats at Geary, west side. Orange-brown brick stack over a tall pale painted-brick ground storey with a plain belt. Brick uppers have a few paired sash windows and a front fire escape of railed balconies near the Geary end. Ground: shop front with sign band at the Geary end, two shuttered square windows, a wide steel gate, an arched door at the north end. Street trees hide the middle of the facade; windows there are inferred from the data. Applied: desaturated tan-brown brick, cream rusticated ground storey, black iron escape, arched entry gets a stone surround, keystone and fanlight, last grille gate removed. Rustication grooves and deeper reveals have no key; the gate at 0.66-0.82 stays (the an iron scissor gate there, not a roll-up). Brick tint desaturated further toward tan-brown. Tint lift (2026-10-02): paint tints lifted toward the sunlit paint (t' = 1-(1-t)k); brick tints converted to target / kit colour. Common-bond brick (more orange than running bond), window hoods as the light stone lintels, denser window columns (trees hide the middle: inferred), scissor gate drawn as an iron lattice instead of a plain door. SKIPPED second arched entry (one arch, the other belongs to the neighbour) and rustication (no key). GroundBand lift (2026-10-03): groundBand tint #efe6d8 -> #f7f2ec (same rule as walls; it was missed by the first colour pass).
